1	# Feishu SVG Whiteboard — Medium Rules
2	
3	These apply to **every** board, regardless of template. A template gives you a **color palette
4	and a mood**; this file is the **hard limits of the medium**. All of it is verified empirically on
5	the real board (the image export and the GUI behave differently — see notes below).
6	
7	## Hard rules
8	
9	- **One font.** The board hardcodes a single font (Noto Sans SC). Never set `font-family`. Type is
10	  size / weight / casing / letter-spacing only — there is no typeface choice.
11	- **Text lives in `<text>` / `<tspan>`** — never outline glyphs as `<path>`.
12	- **Shape vocabulary is native-only — a rectangles-and-circles tool.** Build everything from
13	  `<rect>` (sharp or rounded `rx`), `<circle>`, `<ellipse>`, straight `<line>` / `<polyline>`
14	  connectors, and `<text>` — these become real editable shapes. `<polygon>` and any curved/bezier
15	  `<path>` embed as flat **images** (not shapes, render lumpy) — at most one simple triangle/diamond
16	  as a minor accent, never structural. **No freeform / organic / illustrative shapes** (blobs,
17	  leaves, petals, waves, coral, fans, flowers, stars, confetti, doodles, mascots, "hand-cut"
18	  silhouettes). If a reference is organic, keep only its **palette** and rebuild with rects + circles.
19	- **Arrows = native connectors, never hand-drawn heads.** To put an arrowhead on a line, give the
20	  `<line>` or `<polyline>` a **`marker-end`** (and `marker-start` for a double-headed arrow)
21	  pointing at a `<marker>` in `<defs>`. The board converts these into **native connectors with a
22	  clean built-in arrowhead**, and the arrow takes the line's `stroke` colour. **Never draw an
23	  arrowhead as a separate `<polygon>` / triangle** — a polygon embeds as a flat image and renders
24	  rough, squiggly, and hand-drawn (unprofessional). One marker definition serves the whole board:
25	  ```svg
26	  <defs>
27	    <marker id="arrow" markerWidth="12" markerHeight="12" refX="9" refY="4"
28	            orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth"><path d="M0 0 L10 4 L0 8 z"/></marker>
29	  </defs>
30	  <line x1="100" y1="80" x2="360" y2="80" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
31	  <!-- right-angled connector: polyline (H/V points) + marker-end -->
32	  <polyline points="100,140 240,140 240,220" fill="none" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
33	  <!-- double-headed (e.g. read/write): add marker-start too -->
34	  <line x1="100" y1="280" x2="360" y2="280" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-start="url(#arrow)" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
35	  ```
36	  (The marker's own shape/colour is ignored on the board; it just signals "put a native arrowhead
37	  here." Keep the line straight or right-angled — those map to clean `straight` / `right_angled` connectors.)
38	  **The classic defect** is a `<line>` plus a separate little `<polyline>` / `<polygon>` chevron drawn
39	  at its tip — that chevron IS a hand-drawn arrowhead. Delete it and put `marker-end` on the line.
40	  **Mandatory self-check before you write the board:** run
41	  `grep -nE '<polygon|<polyline' <dir>/diagram.svg` — every `<polygon>`, and every short `<polyline>`
42	  shaped like a triangle/chevron at a line's endpoint, is a defect to convert. (A `<polyline>` is fine
43	  ONLY as a right-angled connector path that itself carries `marker-end` and has no separate chevron.)
44	  **This matters most when you START FROM or EDIT an existing SVG** (a gallery template, a previous
45	  board, a translation): its arrows may predate this rule and still be hand-drawn — re-check and
46	  convert them, don't just edit the text around them.
47	- **Forbidden** (break or flatten to a static image): any gradient, `<filter>`, `<pattern>`,
48	  `<clipPath>`, `<mask>`, blur.
49	- **Opacity is ignored.** `opacity` / `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` all render fully opaque.
50	  To get a paler tint, use a **solid lighter hex** — never alpha. (To fake a translucent overlap,
51	  paint the overlap region as its own solid darker shape.)
52	- **Text color is unrestricted on the live board** (any hex; the GUI's ~9 presets are not a limit) —
53	  **but the image export renders text color unreliably (often black).** Judge text color via
54	  `+query --output_as raw` (stored hex) or the live board, **never** the exported PNG. Light/cream
55	  text works on saturated-dark fills when it's large and bold; small light text on near-black is unreliable.
56	- **Shadows.** No blur/filter shadows (unsupported). Hard **offset shadows are allowed and fine** —
57	  draw one as a **solid duplicate of the SAME shape** offset behind the real one (never a blur). It must
58	  match the element's shape exactly: same `rx` (a pill's shadow is a pill, not a rect), same `width`/`height`,
59	  and inside the same `rotate()` group so it tilts with the element. Default can still be flat — depth also
60	  comes from flat color blocks, role-swaps, and scale.
61	- **No decorative micro-chrome.** No ornamental kicker/footer/slug/metadata labels. Every text
62	  element must be load-bearing and legible (≥ ~16px, strong contrast); keep small text inside
63	  high-contrast panels, never small on a colored canvas.
64	- **Never echo the user's instructions or your own process onto the board.** The board shows the
65	  **content** — never the request that produced it, the inputs you read, or how you built it. A
66	  whiteboard is a finished artifact, not a homework submission, so it carries no "here's what you
67	  asked for" framing. Cut every meta / process line, for example:
68	  - scope or task notes — _"整理范围：仅总结张睿发言；问答部分按她的回答归纳"_, _"本图涵盖第 3-5 章"_
69	  - source citations — _"来源：会议逐字稿 00:06:28–00:52:58 的张睿发言"_, _"based on the attached doc"_
70	  - the chosen style / template name — _"风格：Specimen Bold"_, _"Riso Brut template"_
71	  - audience / format directions, restatements of the prompt, and _"summary of… / 总结自…"_ framing
72	  - dates, tokens, file paths, or tooling you were not explicitly asked to display
73	
74	  A **title may name the subject** (e.g. _"张睿 · 发言总结"_ is fine — that is the topic), but nothing
75	  on the board may describe the task, the source material, or the tool. **Litmus test:** if a line is
76	  addressed to the person who asked (or to a grader) rather than being a real part of the artifact,
77	  delete it. Put that kind of context in your chat reply to the user, never on the canvas.
78	
79	- **Transforms:** `translate` / `rotate` / `scale` are safe; avoid `skewX` / `skewY` / `matrix(...)`.
80	- **No fixed canvas.** No 16:9, no scaler. Work in a logical coordinate space (≈1600–1700 wide) and
81	  let content define the bounds.
82	- **Text reflows by character** (CJK ≈ 1em, Latin ≈ 0.6em). Pad boxes generously; never fit text to
83	  the pixel; wrap long lines across `<tspan>`s rather than shrinking.
84	
85	## Workflow
86	
87	1. Pick a **template** (`templates/<slug>/design.md`) for the palette + mood, and read it.
88	2. Pick the narrative shape (pipeline / stages / comparison / system map / timeline) and write the
89	   SVG in a logical coord space (≈1600–1700 wide); **native shapes only**; every label a `<text>`.
90	3. **Render and LOOK at it — then fix what you see.** This is the most important step:
91	   - `npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg -o <dir>/diagram.png -f svg`
92	   - `npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg -f svg --check`
93	   - **Open `diagram.png` and actually view it.** Correct the common problems before moving on, and
94	     iterate render → look → fix until it's clean:
95	     - **text overflow** — text spilling out of its box or past the canvas edge,
96	     - **margins / padding** — content flush to the canvas edge, or a numeral/title touching a box's
97	       top/side with no breathing room,
98	     - **overlaps** — shapes or labels colliding unintentionally (a duplicate-offset shadow or an
99	       intentional overlap is fine; an accidental one is not),
100	     - **clipping** — anything cut off on the right/bottom.
101	     - **hand-drawn arrowheads** — run `grep -nE '<polygon|<polyline' <dir>/diagram.svg` and convert any
102	       chevron/triangle arrowhead to a `marker-end` (see the Arrows rule above). Do this every time,
103	       and especially when you started from an existing SVG whose arrows may predate the rule.
104	   - (`--check` flags `text-overflow`/`node-overlap`; intentional overlaps, off-canvas bleed, or a
105	     centered long Latin headline may report as warnings — judge with your eyes, not just the linter.)
106	   - **Fix by editing the `.svg` in place with small targeted edits** (nudge a box, widen a panel,
107	     rewrap a label) — never regenerate the whole SVG to fix a local issue, and apply every fix you
108	     spotted in one view in a single edit pass before re-rendering. This keeps the iterate loop cheap
109	     without losing any pass.
110	4. **Write it into Feishu as an editable whiteboard**, then **look at the real board too:**
111	   ```bash
112	   # SVG → whiteboard node JSON → bare nodes array → native editable shapes (colours preserved)
113	   npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg --to openapi --format json -o <dir>/diagram.json
114	   jq '.nodes' <dir>/diagram.json > <dir>/nodes.json
115	   feishu board create-notes <wb_token> --file <dir>/nodes.json --client-token <unique>
116	   feishu board image <wb_token> <dir>/board.png
117	   ```
118	   view `board.png`, and fix any remaining layout issues. The PNG export is faithful for **layout, shapes, fills,
119	   opacity** — but **not text color** (verify colour via `feishu board nodes <wb_token>` raw JSON or the live doc, not the PNG).
120	
121	   Note: `feishu board create-notes` **adds** nodes (no `--overwrite`). Iterate layout in step 3's local
122	   whiteboard-cli PNG render; write to Feishu once near-final. To re-write after a fix, recreate the blank
123	   whiteboard block (delete + re-add) so you start clean, then `create-notes` again.
124	
125	### Creating the doc + whiteboard block to write into
126	
127	If the user didn't give a target whiteboard, create one — a doc with a blank whiteboard block; the
128	response returns `board_tokens` (the whiteboard id to write into):
129	
130	```bash
131	feishu docx create "My board" -c '<whiteboard type="blank"></whiteboard>'
132	# → response includes board_tokens[]; use the first as <wb_token> in step 4
133	```
134	
135	Then write the nodes to that `block_token` with `feishu board create-notes` in step 4. To add a
136	board to an existing doc the user gave, fetch it (`feishu docx read`) or append a
137	`<whiteboard type="blank"></whiteboard>` block (`feishu docx append`/`insert`), and use that block's token.

14	# Beautiful Feishu Whiteboard
15	
16	A design system skill: **35 colour palette styles** plus the verified **hard rules** of the Feishu
17	SVG whiteboard medium, so you can build gorgeous, on brand, _editable_ whiteboards.
18	
19	This is **not** an auto layout chart generator. **You** compose the layout. A template gives you a
20	**palette and mood**; [`RULES.md`](RULES.md) gives you the medium's hard limits. The board you
21	produce is a real, editable Feishu whiteboard inside a doc, not a screenshot.
22	
23	## When to use
24	
25	- The user wants a Feishu / Lark whiteboard, infographic, diagram, poster, or visual explainer that
26	  should look good, branded, or in a specific aesthetic.
27	- The user names a style, or points at one of the templates.
28	- The user gives content ("explain X as a whiteboard", "turn this into a board") and wants it
29	  visual and editable inside Feishu.
30	
31	## Step 0: prerequisites (check before doing anything)
32	
33	Run [`scripts/preflight.sh`](scripts/preflight.sh), or check manually:
34	
35	- **Node 20 or newer.**
36	- **`feishu` CLI** (npm package **`@mi/feishu`**), installed **and authenticated** (replaces lark-cli;
37	  no separate QR/config step). If missing: `npm install -g @mi/feishu`, then `feishu auth login`.
38	- **`@larksuite/whiteboard-cli`**, used via `npx`, auto downloads, no install needed.
39	- A **Feishu / Lark account**. The board is written to the user's own tenant.
40	
41	If the `feishu` CLI is missing or not authenticated, tell the user exactly how to install and
42	authenticate (`npm install -g @mi/feishu` → `feishu auth login`), then stop. You cannot write a board without it.
43	
44	## How to run the conversation
45	
46	1. **Understand the board.** Find out what the user wants on it: the content, the purpose, the
47	   audience. If it is unclear, ask one short question before building.
48	2. **Ask about the vibe.** Ask the user what visual style they want, for example playful or
49	   professional, any colour or mood preference, or a brand to match. Offer to pick for them if they
50	   have no preference. If they already named a style, skip ahead.
51	3. **Pick a style.** Use [`CATALOG.md`](CATALOG.md) to match the content type and the requested vibe
52	   and formality to one of the 35 styles. The catalogue lists each style's palette signature, so
53	   **choose from it alone** — don't open several `design.md` files to compare. Tell the user which
54	   style you chose and why, in one line.
55	4. **Build it.** Read [`RULES.md`](RULES.md) and **only the one** chosen
56	   [`templates/<slug>/design.md`](templates/), then:
57	   - Compose the SVG in a logical space about 1600 to 1700 wide, in that palette, with **native
58	     shapes only** (rect, rounded rect, circle, ellipse, connectors, text). Lay the content out
59	     however reads best. Every label is a `<text>`; never set `font-family`.
60	   - **Only the content goes on the board, never the instruction behind it.** Do not print the
61	     user's prompt, scope notes, source citations, the chosen style name, or any "summary of… /
62	     来源… / 风格…" meta line onto the canvas — that looks like a homework header. Such context
63	     belongs in your chat reply. (See the "Never echo the user's instructions" rule in `RULES.md`.)
64	   - **Render it, then look at the image and correct yourself**: fix text overflow, tight margins or
65	     padding, numerals touching edges, accidental overlaps, and clipping. Iterate render, view, fix
66	     until it is clean. (Commands and the full checklist are in `RULES.md`.) **When fixing, edit the
67	     `.svg` file in place with small targeted edits** (move a box, widen a panel, rewrap a label) —
68	     do not regenerate the whole SVG each pass; and batch the fixes you see in one view into a single
69	     edit pass before re-rendering, rather than one fix per render.
70	   - Write it into a Feishu doc as an editable whiteboard, then view the live board image too and fix
71	     any remaining layout issues.
72	5. **Deliver.** Give the user **both**: the **Feishu doc link** and the **rendered image** itself, so
73	   they can see it without opening the doc. Then tell them they can **switch to a different style**
74	   any time, and you will re render the same content in the new palette.
75	
76	## Files
77	
78	- **[`RULES.md`](RULES.md)**: the hard rules and the exact build, write, and verify commands. Always read this.
79	- **[`CATALOG.md`](CATALOG.md)**: every style with its vibe, formality, and what it is good for. Use it to choose.
80	- **[`templates/<slug>/design.md`](templates/)**: one per style, the colour palette and how to use it.
81	- **[`scripts/preflight.sh`](scripts/preflight.sh)**: dependency and auth check.

1	# Feishu SVG Whiteboard — Medium Rules
2	
3	These apply to **every** board, regardless of template. A template gives you a **color palette
4	and a mood**; this file is the **hard limits of the medium**. All of it is verified empirically on
5	the real board (the image export and the GUI behave differently — see notes below).
6	
7	## Hard rules
8	
9	- **One font.** The board hardcodes a single font (Noto Sans SC). Never set `font-family`. Type is
10	  size / weight / casing / letter-spacing only — there is no typeface choice.
11	- **Text lives in `<text>` / `<tspan>`** — never outline glyphs as `<path>`.
12	- **Shape vocabulary is native-only — a rectangles-and-circles tool.** Build everything from
13	  `<rect>` (sharp or rounded `rx`), `<circle>`, `<ellipse>`, straight `<line>` / `<polyline>`
14	  connectors, and `<text>` — these become real editable shapes. `<polygon>` and any curved/bezier
15	  `<path>` embed as flat **images** (not shapes, render lumpy) — at most one simple triangle/diamond
16	  as a minor accent, never structural. **No freeform / organic / illustrative shapes** (blobs,
17	  leaves, petals, waves, coral, fans, flowers, stars, confetti, doodles, mascots, "hand-cut"
18	  silhouettes). If a reference is organic, keep only its **palette** and rebuild with rects + circles.
19	- **Arrows = native connectors, never hand-drawn heads.** To put an arrowhead on a line, give the
20	  `<line>` or `<polyline>` a **`marker-end`** (and `marker-start` for a double-headed arrow)
21	  pointing at a `<marker>` in `<defs>`. The board converts these into **native connectors with a
22	  clean built-in arrowhead**, and the arrow takes the line's `stroke` colour. **Never draw an
23	  arrowhead as a separate `<polygon>` / triangle** — a polygon embeds as a flat image and renders
24	  rough, squiggly, and hand-drawn (unprofessional). One marker definition serves the whole board:
25	  ```svg
26	  <defs>
27	    <marker id="arrow" markerWidth="12" markerHeight="12" refX="9" refY="4"
28	            orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth"><path d="M0 0 L10 4 L0 8 z"/></marker>
29	  </defs>
30	  <line x1="100" y1="80" x2="360" y2="80" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
31	  <!-- right-angled connector: polyline (H/V points) + marker-end -->
32	  <polyline points="100,140 240,140 240,220" fill="none" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
33	  <!-- double-headed (e.g. read/write): add marker-start too -->
34	  <line x1="100" y1="280" x2="360" y2="280" stroke="#0D4FA8" stroke-width="3" marker-start="url(#arrow)" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
35	  ```
36	  (The marker's own shape/colour is ignored on the board; it just signals "put a native arrowhead
37	  here." Keep the line straight or right-angled — those map to clean `straight` / `right_angled` connectors.)
38	  **The classic defect** is a `<line>` plus a separate little `<polyline>` / `<polygon>` chevron drawn
39	  at its tip — that chevron IS a hand-drawn arrowhead. Delete it and put `marker-end` on the line.
40	  **Mandatory self-check before you write the board:** run
41	  `grep -nE '<polygon|<polyline' <dir>/diagram.svg` — every `<polygon>`, and every short `<polyline>`
42	  shaped like a triangle/chevron at a line's endpoint, is a defect to convert. (A `<polyline>` is fine
43	  ONLY as a right-angled connector path that itself carries `marker-end` and has no separate chevron.)
44	  **This matters most when you START FROM or EDIT an existing SVG** (a gallery template, a previous
45	  board, a translation): its arrows may predate this rule and still be hand-drawn — re-check and
46	  convert them, don't just edit the text around them.
47	- **Forbidden** (break or flatten to a static image): any gradient, `<filter>`, `<pattern>`,
48	  `<clipPath>`, `<mask>`, blur.
49	- **Opacity is ignored.** `opacity` / `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` all render fully opaque.
50	  To get a paler tint, use a **solid lighter hex** — never alpha. (To fake a translucent overlap,
51	  paint the overlap region as its own solid darker shape.)
52	- **Text color is unrestricted on the live board** (any hex; the GUI's ~9 presets are not a limit) —
53	  **but the image export renders text color unreliably (often black).** Judge text color via
54	  `+query --output_as raw` (stored hex) or the live board, **never** the exported PNG. Light/cream
55	  text works on saturated-dark fills when it's large and bold; small light text on near-black is unreliable.
56	- **Shadows.** No blur/filter shadows (unsupported). Hard **offset shadows are allowed and fine** —
57	  draw one as a **solid duplicate of the SAME shape** offset behind the real one (never a blur). It must
58	  match the element's shape exactly: same `rx` (a pill's shadow is a pill, not a rect), same `width`/`height`,
59	  and inside the same `rotate()` group so it tilts with the element. Default can still be flat — depth also
60	  comes from flat color blocks, role-swaps, and scale.
61	- **No decorative micro-chrome.** No ornamental kicker/footer/slug/metadata labels. Every text
62	  element must be load-bearing and legible (≥ ~16px, strong contrast); keep small text inside
63	  high-contrast panels, never small on a colored canvas.
64	- **Never echo the user's instructions or your own process onto the board.** The board shows the
65	  **content** — never the request that produced it, the inputs you read, or how you built it. A
66	  whiteboard is a finished artifact, not a homework submission, so it carries no "here's what you
67	  asked for" framing. Cut every meta / process line, for example:
68	  - scope or task notes — _"整理范围：仅总结张睿发言；问答部分按她的回答归纳"_, _"本图涵盖第 3-5 章"_
69	  - source citations — _"来源：会议逐字稿 00:06:28–00:52:58 的张睿发言"_, _"based on the attached doc"_
70	  - the chosen style / template name — _"风格：Specimen Bold"_, _"Riso Brut template"_
71	  - audience / format directions, restatements of the prompt, and _"summary of… / 总结自…"_ framing
72	  - dates, tokens, file paths, or tooling you were not explicitly asked to display
73	
74	  A **title may name the subject** (e.g. _"张睿 · 发言总结"_ is fine — that is the topic), but nothing
75	  on the board may describe the task, the source material, or the tool. **Litmus test:** if a line is
76	  addressed to the person who asked (or to a grader) rather than being a real part of the artifact,
77	  delete it. Put that kind of context in your chat reply to the user, never on the canvas.
78	
79	- **Transforms:** `translate` / `rotate` / `scale` are safe; avoid `skewX` / `skewY` / `matrix(...)`.
80	- **No fixed canvas.** No 16:9, no scaler. Work in a logical coordinate space (≈1600–1700 wide) and
81	  let content define the bounds.
82	- **Text reflows by character** (CJK ≈ 1em, Latin ≈ 0.6em). Pad boxes generously; never fit text to
83	  the pixel; wrap long lines across `<tspan>`s rather than shrinking.
84	
85	## Workflow
86	
87	1. Pick a **template** (`templates/<slug>/design.md`) for the palette + mood, and read it.
88	2. Pick the narrative shape (pipeline / stages / comparison / system map / timeline) and write the
89	   SVG in a logical coord space (≈1600–1700 wide); **native shapes only**; every label a `<text>`.
90	3. **Render and LOOK at it — then fix what you see.** This is the most important step:
91	   - `npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg -o <dir>/diagram.png -f svg`
92	   - `npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg -f svg --check`
93	   - **Open `diagram.png` and actually view it.** Correct the common problems before moving on, and
94	     iterate render → look → fix until it's clean:
95	     - **text overflow** — text spilling out of its box or past the canvas edge,
96	     - **margins / padding** — content flush to the canvas edge, or a numeral/title touching a box's
97	       top/side with no breathing room,
98	     - **overlaps** — shapes or labels colliding unintentionally (a duplicate-offset shadow or an
99	       intentional overlap is fine; an accidental one is not),
100	     - **clipping** — anything cut off on the right/bottom.
101	     - **hand-drawn arrowheads** — run `grep -nE '<polygon|<polyline' <dir>/diagram.svg` and convert any
102	       chevron/triangle arrowhead to a `marker-end` (see the Arrows rule above). Do this every time,
103	       and especially when you started from an existing SVG whose arrows may predate the rule.
104	   - (`--check` flags `text-overflow`/`node-overlap`; intentional overlaps, off-canvas bleed, or a
105	     centered long Latin headline may report as warnings — judge with your eyes, not just the linter.)
106	   - **Fix by editing the `.svg` in place with small targeted edits** (nudge a box, widen a panel,
107	     rewrap a label) — never regenerate the whole SVG to fix a local issue, and apply every fix you
108	     spotted in one view in a single edit pass before re-rendering. This keeps the iterate loop cheap
109	     without losing any pass.
110	4. **Write it into Feishu as an editable whiteboard**, then **look at the real board too:**
111	   ```bash
112	   # SVG → whiteboard node JSON → bare nodes array → native editable shapes (colours preserved)
113	   npx -y @larksuite/whiteboard-cli@^0.2.11 -i <dir>/diagram.svg --to openapi --format json -o <dir>/diagram.json
114	   jq '.nodes' <dir>/diagram.json > <dir>/nodes.json
115	   feishu board create-notes <wb_token> --file <dir>/nodes.json --client-token <unique>
116	   feishu board image <wb_token> <dir>/board.png
117	   ```
118	   view `board.png`, and fix any remaining layout issues. The PNG export is faithful for **layout, shapes, fills,
119	   opacity** — but **not text color** (verify colour via `feishu board nodes <wb_token>` raw JSON or the live doc, not the PNG).
120	
121	   Note: `feishu board create-notes` **adds** nodes (no `--overwrite`). Iterate layout in step 3's local
122	   whiteboard-cli PNG render; write to Feishu once near-final. To re-write after a fix, recreate the blank
123	   whiteboard block (delete + re-add) so you start clean, then `create-notes` again.
124	
125	### Creating the doc + whiteboard block to write into
126	
127	If the user didn't give a target whiteboard, create one — a doc with a blank whiteboard block; the
128	response returns `board_tokens` (the whiteboard id to write into):
129	
130	```bash
131	feishu docx create "My board" -c '<whiteboard type="blank"></whiteboard>'
132	# → response includes board_tokens[]; use the first as <wb_token> in step 4
133	```
134	
135	Then write the nodes to that `block_token` with `feishu board create-notes` in step 4. To add a
136	board to an existing doc the user gave, fetch it (`feishu docx read`) or append a
137	`<whiteboard type="blank"></whiteboard>` block (`feishu docx append`/`insert`), and use that block's token.

---
name: document-formatting
description: >
  文档排版与美化。One skill covering three document typesetting/beautification capabilities —
  (1) safely formatting and updating Feishu/Lark docs through MCP (table widths/alignment, Markdown
  emphasis, section-scoped edits, punctuation-locale consistency, async write verification);
  (2) authoring diagram-first technical documentation from fragmented notes, diffs, logs, or
  measurements (converting flat prose/tables into Mermaid or ASCII text-sketches); (3) building
  beautiful, editable Feishu/Lark whiteboards, infographics, posters and visual explainers from SVG
  using a 35-style colour-palette library. Use when the user wants to format, restyle, or beautify a
  document, lay out a technical report, turn prose into diagrams, or create a polished Feishu
  whiteboard/poster/infographic.
---

# Document Formatting (文档排版美化)

One skill, three capabilities. Dispatch by what the user is actually asking for, then read only the
reference files that capability needs.

| The user wants… | Capability | Read first |
|---|---|---|
| Format / restyle / safely edit an existing Feishu doc (tables, bold, sections, punctuation) | **A. Feishu formatting & safe update** | [references/formatting-rules.md](references/formatting-rules.md) |
| Turn notes / diffs / logs / prose into readable technical documentation, with diagrams | **B. Diagram-first documentation** | [references/diagram-selection.md](references/diagram-selection.md) |
| A beautiful editable Feishu whiteboard / infographic / poster | **C. Beautiful whiteboard** | [whiteboard/RULES.md](whiteboard/RULES.md) + [whiteboard/CATALOG.md](whiteboard/CATALOG.md) |

A single request can cross capabilities (e.g. "write up this investigation as a Feishu doc with
diagrams and make it look good") — then apply **B** to author the canonical Markdown, **A** to adapt
and write it safely, and **C** only if a standalone whiteboard/poster is wanted.

---

## Capability A — Feishu formatting & safe update

**Core contract.** Format by visible content and semantic role, then mutate the **smallest complete
structural block** in document order. An MCP success response is not completion: every completed
mutation batch must survive read-back with tables, code, diagrams, media, and neighbors intact.
User-explicit styling overrides defaults. Content skills decide facts; this capability controls
serialization, layout, update safety, and verification.

**Workflow (condensed):**

1. **Fetch and classify.** Call `fetch_doc` without `limit`/`offset` to get the complete document,
   then locate boundaries locally. Never infer current headings/tokens from an old draft.
2. **Build a structural manifest** in document order: headings; table boundaries/shape; fenced code
   and Mermaid boundaries; callout/grid/container boundaries; whiteboard/image/file tokens, order,
   and neighbors; target/preserve status. Never split a table/fence/container or cross media.
3. **Allocate auditable table widths** to the document's *actual* text-column width (≈800px
   narrow, ≈930px wide). Width count = column count, sum = chosen total. Center headers/compact
   values; leave paths/prose left-aligned. Vertical centering is **UI-only** — never claim it from a write.
4. **Preflight serialization** (balanced fences, equal cells per row, same-block bold, punctuation
   locale). CJK context → full-width marks; pure-ASCII context → ASCII mark + space; never mix;
   code/ASCII fences exempt.
5. **Mutate in document order.** No `overwrite`/`replace_all` on existing docs. Use one unique
   complete-block `replace_range`, precise inserts, or true-end append. Escape literal `...` as `\.\.\.`.
6. **Resolve async completion.** A `task_id` is not completion — poll the same tool to terminal state.
7. **Read-back barrier** after every batch: re-fetch the affected block + neighbors and verify.

**Hard rules (non-negotiable):** no existing-doc `overwrite`/`replace_all`; no non-unique or
speculative selection; no split structural block or media crossing; no width-count/sum mismatch; no
blanket centering of paths/prose; no mixed punctuation locales; no next batch before async
completion + read-back; no rendering-success claim from MCP acceptance alone.

Full detail (operation table, width policy, lark-table structure, bold safety, selection safety,
ordered async batches, red flags) is in [references/formatting-rules.md](references/formatting-rules.md).

---

## Capability B — Diagram-first documentation

**Core principle.** Organize around the reader's questions, not the author's chronology. Use diagrams
only where they compress structure or causality better than prose, and keep every claim tied to
evidence. A diagram reads as authoritative, so precision matters more than in prose — never let a
visual encode a vague, guessed, or unverified condition/threshold/step.

**Two task shapes.** (a) Author a new document from raw notes/diffs/logs. (b) **Convert** existing
flat prose or tables into diagrams on request (e.g. "文字不生动，绘制图形表示原理和流程") — preserve
facts, exact labels, and neighbouring rich content; change only the targeted block; add at most one
takeaway; do not duplicate an adjacent diagram.

**Workflow (condensed):**

1. **Fix goal and scope.** Audience, review goal, supplied evidence, desired output, target.
2. **Inventory evidence** as Fact / Interpretation / Decision / Limit — never smooth uncertainty into fact.
3. **Map reader questions → evidence → best visual → exact-value table → limiting evidence.**
4. **Build the terminology ladder** before technical wording: `plain meaning → technical term → exact source label`.
5. **Choose one evidence-backed visual per question.** Mermaid for rendered flow/sequence/state; a
   fenced **ASCII text-sketch** for precise inline annotation, lanes/layout/funnel/compact state
   machines. A table stays a table only for exact parallel values/mappings.
6. **Compose to a proportional reading budget** (10s / 1min / deep review).
7. **Produce the canonical platform-neutral Markdown first**; adapt to Feishu only when requested
   (see [references/feishu-adapter.md](references/feishu-adapter.md)).

**Budgets.** Short or single-mechanism note: **1–3 diagrams**, ~900-word ceiling, no minimum. Long or
multi-stage handoff: count by distinct reader questions (**4–7 typical, not a quota**), no word
ceiling; diagrams ≥ tables for process-heavy content. For a Chinese long-form deep doc, title with
**“深度梳理”**, not **“交接”/“技术交接”**.

Full detail (visual selection table, complexity budgets, Mermaid + text-sketch patterns, evidence
classes, reading-budget shapes) is in [references/diagram-selection.md](references/diagram-selection.md).
Run every objective gate in [references/readability-gates.md](references/readability-gates.md) before
delivery. Feishu adaptation rules are in [references/feishu-adapter.md](references/feishu-adapter.md).

---

## Capability C — Beautiful Feishu whiteboard

A design-system skill: **35 colour-palette styles** plus the verified hard rules of the Feishu SVG
whiteboard medium. This is **not** an auto-layout chart generator — **you** compose the layout; a
template gives palette + mood, [`whiteboard/RULES.md`](whiteboard/RULES.md) gives the medium's hard
limits. The output is a real, editable Feishu whiteboard inside a doc, not a screenshot.

**How to run:**

1. **Check prerequisites** first — run `whiteboard/scripts/preflight.sh` (Node ≥20, `feishu` CLI
   `@mi/feishu` installed + authenticated, `@larksuite/whiteboard-cli` via npx). Stop with install
   instructions if missing.
2. **Understand the board** (content, purpose, audience), then **ask about the vibe** (playful vs
   professional, colour/mood, brand) unless already named.
3. **Pick a style** from [`whiteboard/CATALOG.md`](whiteboard/CATALOG.md) alone (palette signatures
   listed there — do not open several `design.md` to compare). Say which and why, in one line.
4. **Build** — read [`whiteboard/RULES.md`](whiteboard/RULES.md) and only the one chosen
   `whiteboard/templates/<slug>/design.md`, then compose the SVG (~1600–1700 logical width, **native
   shapes only**: rect/rounded-rect/circle/ellipse/line/polyline + `<text>`; arrows via `marker-end`,
   never hand-drawn `<polygon>` heads; no gradient/filter/pattern/opacity/shadows; never set
   `font-family`). **Only content goes on the board, never the instruction/meta behind it.** Render,
   **look at the image, fix what you see** (overflow, margins, overlaps, clipping, hand-drawn
   arrowheads) via small in-place SVG edits. Then write into Feishu with `feishu board create-notes`
   and view the live board too.
5. **Deliver both** the Feishu doc link **and** the rendered image, and offer to switch styles.

The hard medium rules (one font, native shapes, arrow markers, opacity ignored, no shadows, no
echoing the user's instructions, reflow-by-character) live in
[whiteboard/RULES.md](whiteboard/RULES.md). The full 35-style catalogue (level / formality / vibe /
palette hex) is [whiteboard/CATALOG.md](whiteboard/CATALOG.md); per-style palette notes are in
[whiteboard/templates/](whiteboard/templates/); preview images in
[whiteboard/assets/styles/](whiteboard/assets/styles/).

---

## Cross-capability guardrails

- **Source of truth is one.** Author canonical Markdown (B) first; Feishu (A/C) is a rendering and
  placement target, never a second source of truth.
- **Preserve rich content.** Never destroy media, whiteboards, comments, or collaborative structure
  to edit nearby text; keep selections narrow.
- **Never publish silently.** Default to draft + preview; verify after every write.
- **Facts vs layout.** The document's facts come from the evidence; this skill controls layout,
  serialization, update safety, and visual polish — not truth.

3	
4	Patterns and assembled fragments only — no full secret literals in this file.
5	Writes reuse the same inode (open('w')) so a live appender keeps working.

14	import re

20	    try:
21	        with open(os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/settings.mimo.json")) as f:
22	            return json.load(f)["env"]["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"]
23	    except Exception:

26	# (regex-or-string, replacement, label)
27	SUBS = [
28	    (re.compile(r"<REDACTED:jira-pat-prefix>[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+"), "<REDACTED:jira-pat>", "jira-pat"),
29	    (re.compile(r"mcp_u-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}"), "<REDACTED:gerrit-mcp-token>", "gerrit-mcp"),
30	    ("-".join(["<REDACTED:volc>", "8cbe", "4ef6", "9a18", "<REDACTED:volc>"]), "<REDACTED:volc-key>", "volc-key"),
31	    # Split-fragment forms (printf $1..$5 / "-".join([...]) / V4=... V2=...) survive full-key
32	    # matching; the 8-char head and 12-char tail alone identify the key, so scrub them too.
33	    ("<REDACTED:volc>", "<REDACTED:volc>", "volc-frag-head"),
34	    ("<REDACTED:volc>", "<REDACTED:volc>", "volc-frag-tail"),
35	    ("<REDACTED:emu-frag>" + "<REDACTED:emu-frag>", "<REDACTED:emulator-console-token>", "emu-token"),
36	    (re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}"), "<REDACTED:github-token>", "github"),
37	    (re.compile(r"sk-ya[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"), "<REDACTED:mify-key>", "mify-key"),
38	    ("zy" + "236975", "<REDACTED:sudo-pw>", "sudo-pw"),
39	    ("deskmate/<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "deskmate/<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "mqtt-pw-1"),
40	    (re.compile(r"MQTT_PASSWORD=<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>"), "MQTT_PASSWORD=<REDACTED:mqtt-pw>", "mqtt-pw-2"),
41	]
42	m = mimo_token()
43	if m:
44	    SUBS.append((m, "<REDACTED:mimo-gw-token>", "mimo-gw-token"))
45	
46	# ── Split-fragment forms that survive the regexes above (2026-10-12 lesson) ──
47	def _A(*parts): return "".join(parts)
48	_GERRIT  = _A("<REDACTED:gerrit-frag>","81F4GDYx1e9G","04pYl_C5tb","HQ9TNFEyB3giKQ")
49	_JSECRET = _A("7FMrGdPlZw","F<REDACTED:jira-pat-frag>")
50	_MIFY = ""
51	try:
52	    _kp = os.path.join(HOME, "桌面/tmp/key.txt")
53	    if os.path.exists(_kp):
54	        _MIFY = open(_kp).read().strip()
55	except Exception:
56	    pass
57	SUBS += [

59	    (_GERRIT[:18], "<REDACTED:gerrit-frag>", "gerrit-head18"),
60	    (_GERRIT[18:], "<REDACTED:gerrit-frag>", "gerrit-tail26"),
61	    ("<REDACTED:gerrit-frag>", "<REDACTED:gerrit-frag>", "gerrit-head7"),
62	    (_JSECRET, "<REDACTED:jira-pat-frag>", "jira-secret"),
63	    (_JSECRET[:11], "<REDACTED:jira-pat-frag>", "jira-secret-head"),
64	    (_JSECRET[11:], "<REDACTED:jira-pat-frag>", "jira-secret-tail"),
65	    (_A("NjYxNzc1MzY0","MjU0Oj"), "<REDACTED:jira-pat-prefix>", "jira-pat-prefix"),

74	        (_MIFY[-8:], "<REDACTED:mify-frag>", "mify-tail8"),

83	        return len(pat.findall(s))
84	    return s.count(pat)
